text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 4.4% today as oil prices surged to six-month highs amid escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude topped $116 per barrel—driven by reports that the U.S. is preparing strikes against Iran and pulling diplomats from Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks on oil infrastructure. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly translate to higher profits on the barrels it produces and sells.

This move fits into a two-week rally of 13% that tracks closely with a sharp climb in global oil prices as geopolitical risk in the Middle East has intensified. Supply disruptions or conflict in that region threaten to tighten global oil markets, which historically benefits large producers more than it helps consumers or refiners.
